drafted_from: tools/meaning-search/tool-rows.json (tool:make-a-vector-set-from-picture-vectors-my-apps-kept), do-work/make_vector_set_from_kept_vectors.py and test/kept_vectors_check.py (asset_index fixture); the answer was produced by running the script on that fixture
start_here: Say to your AI: "Turn the picture vectors my asset index already kept into sets I can search by what the pictures show, and put them in a new folder."
no_lists_because: It keeps no list: it only reads the stores of vectors you name on this computer and writes a folder of files for each.
instructions: 1. Find the stores your programs kept: an asset index folder (clip-video-embeddings.npy, clip-video-ids.json, clip-embeddings.npy, clip-ids.json, assets.jsonl), a folder with frames.npy and frames.jsonl, or an app's SQLite results store. They are only read.

2. The AI reads this tool's row with tools:list, then runs on your computer: python3 trillion-workshop/tools/meaning-search/do-work/make_vector_set_from_kept_vectors.py --asset-index <folder> --out <new folder>. Add --ssd-index, --expansion-results, --namespace or --kind video|image|all for other stores.

3. Read the last line: {"result": {"sets": {"<set name>": <item count>}}}, or {"error": ...} when no store was given. Each set is a folder under --out with items.jsonl, vectors.npy and vector-set.json.

4. Put each vector-set.json's vector_set, with the model that made the vectors (the same model tool:words-as-picture-vector uses for your words), into a semantic-index-descriptor record, then search with tool:find-similar-to-a-vector or across sets with tool:find-closest-across-my-indexes.

worked_examples.title: An asset index with two videos and one image becomes two sets
worked_examples.ask: Turn the picture vectors my asset index already kept into sets I can search by what the pictures show.
worked_examples.given: From test/kept_vectors_check.py (its asset_index fixture) and do-work/make_vector_set_from_kept_vectors.py, run on this computer. The folder assets holds clip-video-embeddings.npy [[3,4],[0,2]], clip-video-ids.json ["/made/up/one.mp4","/made/up/two.mp4"], clip-embeddings.npy [[1,0]], clip-ids.json ["/made/up/still.jpg"] and assets.jsonl naming /made/up/one.mp4 as "Folder/One.mp4". The command the AI runs after reading the row: python3 trillion-workshop/tools/meaning-search/do-work/make_vector_set_from_kept_vectors.py --asset-index assets --out sets
worked_examples.hands_back: {"result": {"sets": {"asset-index-video": 2, "asset-index-image": 1}}} is the last line. sets/asset-index-video/items.jsonl holds {"path": "/made/up/one.mp4", "kind": "video-frame", "t": null, "name": "Folder/One.mp4"} and {"path": "/made/up/two.mp4", "kind": "video-frame", "t": null, "name": "two.mp4"}; its vectors.npy is float16 and normalised (the first row is [0.6, 0.8]); its vector-set.json has points_to {"file": "path", "start": "t", "carry": ["kind", "name"]} and "items": 2.
